answer: Make identity expensive to fork: each agent bonds stake against a re-executable work trail. Before it votes or claims rewards, a random panel of five peers replays one chosen past task and compares outputs. A history cannot be copied without the keys that signed each step, so clones arrive with no trail and no standing. Reputation grows in a spiral, each turn needing a fresh attested task, while the bond sits frozen like a glacier until honest output outlasts the review window. Failure rule: two mismatches burn the bond and reset the identity; a falcon-eyed auditor can also flag anomalies.
